en: *Petavatthu*, Ubbarivagga, 12. The Story of Kaṇṇamuṇḍa [The hungry ghost] with ears like mushrooms appeared before me. I asked him: "Who are you? He replied: "I am a hungry ghost. "By what deed did you come to this state? Tell me, O hungry ghost. "I was a woman who lived in Benares; I was known as Kaṇṇamuṇḍā. I was beautiful, charming, and possessed of great splendor. I was devoted to my husband, faithful, and well-behaved. But my mother-in-law and father-in-law were harsh toward me. They would constantly strike me with sticks and clods of earth. And they would say: 'This woman is wicked and shameless. Because of that evil deed, I have fallen into this state. I am tormented by hunger and thirst; I am suffering greatly. I am not able to obtain even a drop of water. If one gives alms to a monk, or to a nun, or to a male or female lay follower, or to a person who has gone forth, it will bring great fruit. Therefore, give alms to those who have gone forth. Give food and drink to the monks. Give clothing and bedding to the nuns. Then you will attain happiness in the world of the gods. Thus spoke the hungry ghost Kaṇṇamuṇḍa. Having heard his words, I gave alms to the monks. I gave food and drink, and also clothing and bedding. Because of that merit, I have attained a fortunate rebirth.

I dwell in the world of the gods, enjoying celestial bliss. May you also give alms to the monks. Give food and drink, and also clothing and bedding. Then you too shall attain happiness in the world of the gods. Thus spoke the hungry ghost Kaṇṇamuṇḍa. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was staying at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then a certain man approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to the Blessed One: "Venerable sir, why is it that some women here are ugly, unattractive, and lacking in splendor, while others are beautiful, attractive, and possessed of great splendor? The Blessed One replied: "Householder, it is because of their own deeds that some women here are ugly, unattractive, and lacking in splendor, while others are beautiful, attractive, and possessed of great splendor. Householder, there are four kinds of women. What four? The woman who is devoted to her husband, faithful, and well-behaved, but who is struck by her mother-in-law and father-in-law with sticks and clods of earth, and who is told: 'This woman is wicked and shameless'—because of that evil deed, she falls into such a state. But the woman who is devoted to her husband, faithful, and well-behaved, and who gives alms to monks and nuns, and provides them with food, drink, clothing, and bedding—because of that merit, she attains a fortunate rebirth and dwells in the world of the gods, enjoying celestial bliss. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and departed. Then that man, having heard the Blessed One's words, went to his own home and addressed his wife: "My dear, from today onward, you must give alms to the monks and nuns, and provide them with food, drink, clothing, and bedding. "Yes, master," she replied. From then on, she gave alms to the monks and nuns, and provided them with food, drink, clothing, and bedding. Because of that merit, she attained a fortunate rebirth and dwelt in the world of the gods, enjoying celestial bliss. Thus have I heard. With stair-treads of gold and floors spread with golden sand,
there [stood] the lovely Sogandhiya grove.
Pleasingly fragrant and delightful,
covered with various trees and stirred by diverse scents.
Covered with various lotuses and strewn with white lilies,
they waft forth a fragrant scent.
Pleasant, stirred by the breeze,
and resounding with the cries of swans and cranes,
and the warbling of ruddy geese.
Crowded with various kinds of birds,
endowed with various groups of lakes,
and bearing various kinds of fruits are the trees.
Forests bearing various flowers.
Among humans, there is no city such as this one.
Many palaces are yours,
made of gold and silver;
they shine forth, resplendent.
In all four directions.
You have five hundred female slaves who serve as your attendants.
Wearing shells and armlets,
adorned with golden earrings—
many such couches are yours.
Made of gold and silver,
covered with kadali-deer skins,
and spread with woolen blankets.
Wherever you have taken up residence,
O lady who has all your desires fulfilled,
having reached the middle of the night—
Then, having risen, you depart.
Having gone to the park grounds,
[you look] all around the lotus pond;
You stood upon its bank,
on pleasant, green grass;
then a dog with cropped ears [attacked] you.
It devours limb after limb;
and when it has been devoured,
it is made into a skeleton of bones.
You have entered the lotus pond,
and your body has become as it was before;
thus, you are now possessed of all your limbs and members.
Beautiful and lovely to behold,
having clothed herself in a garment,
she came into my presence.
What indeed has been done wrongly by body, speech, or mind?
Through the ripening of what karma...
“Kannamuṇḍa the dog is devouring your limbs, householder. “What of it, Kimala? [he replied].
He was a faithful lay follower;
I was his wife,
immoral and unfaithful.
As I was passing by,
my husband said this to me:
“This is not fitting, nor is it proper.”
"You who transgress against me!"—
thus I uttered a terrible oath and spoke a falsehood.
‘I do not transgress against you,
whether by body or by mind.
If I were to transgress against you, [then...’”
With body and with mind,
let this dog Kaṇṇamuṇḍa devour my limbs one by one.
As the ripening of that karma,
and for both [types of] false speech,
for exactly five hundred years,
For this has been experienced by me:
the dog Kaṇṇamuṇḍa is devouring my limbs one by one.
And you, O Lord, have been a great benefactor,
having come here for my sake;
I am well liberated from Kaṇṇamuṇḍa.
Free from sorrow and fearless from any quarter—
those I revere, O King,
with palms joined in supplication; I entreat you.
“Enjoy superhuman pleasures;
delight, O god, together with me.
“Superhuman pleasures have been enjoyed;”
"I am delighted to be with you;
therefore, O fortunate one, I entreat you:
quickly give me back my mind."
The Story of the Kaṇṇamuṇḍa Ghost, the Twelfth.
